messages:
anya.k: Quick question — who is the true source of truth for traffic splits and guards? The console has rollout policies, but our feature-flag service also supports weighted flags. Confusing for customers and engineers.
matt.p: Short answer: we never intended both to act independently. Rollout policies should be authoritative for deployments; flags are feature switches. But we don't have strict enforcement today.
sasha.r: This is causing metrics confusion too. Dashboards show traffic by flag key and by rollout id, and they diverge when both are set. Hard to tell which drove the user bucket.
jude.l: Agree. Proposal: explicit precedence + a validator in the API. If a request includes a rollout_id, runtime should prefer policy routing. If only flag is present, use flag. And warn if both are present.
anya.k: Sounds reasonable. What about console UX? We need to show where a split is coming from. Currently it just lists "active splits" and doesn't explain layering.
matt.p: Console change: add a small badge on splits that indicates origin: [policy] or [flag]. Click expands the config stack with a one-line precedence rule.
sasha.r: Also need telemetry: tag events with routing_source=policy|flag and include rollout_id/flag_key. That makes dashboards unambiguous.
jude.l: For enforcement, suggest an API-level rejection when both are set and they conflict unless caller sets `allow_override=true` and documents reason. Prevents accidental shadowing.
anya.k: Can we show an inline example in the API doc? Something like:
```json
POST /v1/infer
{
  "model": "redwood-gpt-13b",
  "rollout_id": "canary-2027-03",
  "feature_flags": {"new-tokenizer": 50}
}
```
And then a note: `rollout_id` wins over flag-percentage unless `allow_override=true`.
matt.p: Exactly. Also runtime should emit a `routing_decision` object in the response headers (for internal calls) so internal tools can correlate without parsing logs. e.g., `X-Routing-Decision: policy:canary-2027-03;source=policy`
sasha.r: We'll need a migration plan for existing dashboards. Maybe a compatibility mode where flags are mapped to synthetic rollout_ids for N months.
jude.l: +1 on compatibility mode. Also add a lint/CI check in infra: if console rollout and flag mapping both exist for same target path, CI warns.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-policy-clarity-docs -> staging (ETA 12m) :rocket:
anya.k: Thanks. Can we capture this as an RFC? I'll draft one and include the precedence table, API changes, telemetry fields, and console UX mocks. Will @matt.p @sasha.r @jude.l review? :pray:
matt.p: Yes, happy to review.
sasha.r: I'll sketch dashboard migration notes.
jude.l: I'll add the validator + unit tests plan.
anya.k: Great, thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link when ready.
